=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: text_field() function (lines 586-595) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The `text_field()` helper does not sanitize all delimiter markers and embedded backticks in untrusted prior-finding fields.
  WHY: A malicious or malformed prior finding could spoof prompt delimiters or alter prompt structure; severity was reported as MAJOR by mistralai_mistral-small-2603, while minimax_minimax-m3 characterized the project-specification delimiter case as hardening-only.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: prior-findings validation (lines 595-615) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The Python validator for `SECURITY_AUDIT_PRIOR_FINDINGS` rejects absolute paths and `..` path segments but does not normalize leading `./` before adding cited files to audit scope.
  WHY: The delta re-audit may silently drop re-emitted findings or fail closed when the stored file field contains `./file.py` while the changed-file list contains `file.py`.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: delta scope narrowing (lines 485-516) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: When `SECURITY_AUDIT_DIFF_SINCE` is set but the intersection with changed files is empty, the script creates an empty `CHANGED_FILES_FILE.delta` and proceeds without explicit handling to ensure at least one file remains in scope.
  WHY: The audit may proceed with an empty file list, causing the model to receive no scope constraints and potentially report findings outside the intended range.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: log prefix SECURITY_PASS_SCOPE (line 550) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The new log prefix `SECURITY_PASS_SCOPE` is emitted by the poller but is not registered in the stable `LOG_PREFIX.name` list in `agents.md`.
  WHY: Downstream parsers and workflow-log-analysis tooling that rely on the contractual registry will not recognize the new prefix, causing parsing failures or missed telemetry.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Location: text_field() (lines 586-595)
  Issue: The sanitization loop only neutralises the two `=== BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED PRIOR FINDINGS ===` markers. A crafted finding whose `exploit_scenario` carries `=== BEGIN UNTRUSTED PROJECT SPECIFICATION ===` would render verbatim inside the still-open PRIOR FINDINGS fence (the project-specification block is rendered later in the same `security_audit_append_prompt_context()` call). With the current prompt ordering the spoof cannot escape the untrusted block, so this is hardening-only.
  Suggested minimal fix: extend the `for untrusted_fence in (...)` tuple to include `("=== BEGIN UNTRUSTED PROJECT SPECIFICATION ===", "=== END UNTRUSTED PROJECT SPECIFICATION ===")` so the same `replace(untrusted_fence, "[untrusted marker removed]")` neutralises both fences uniformly.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  SEVERITY: MAJOR
